back: A planning technique that shows the activities of a project, their order and duration, so that the minimum completion time and the activities that cannot be delayed can be found.
The longest route through the network. Its activities have zero float, so a delay to any of them delays the whole project.
An activity of zero duration, used to show that one activity depends on another.
Earliest start = largest earliest finish of the activities that precede it. Earliest finish = earliest start + duration.
Latest finish = smallest latest start of the activities that follow it. Latest start = latest finish - duration.
Total float = latest start - earliest start (the delay possible without delaying the project). Critical activities have zero.
Free float = earliest start of the following activity - earliest finish of this one. It cannot exceed total float.
The largest earliest finish in the network, which is also the length of the critical path.
Benefits: shows the minimum time and critical jobs, helps schedule resources and manage delays. Limits: depends on estimated durations, takes time to update, may give false precision.
Reducing a critical activity shortens the project only until another route becomes equally long; after that there is no further saving.
